findings.title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called here, but this file has no `prisma` import. Type checking/building the app-store package will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, blocking the application build.

findings.title: The fallback token schema discards every expiry field from sync responses
findings.body: Both computed property names evaluate to the same string (`"[object Object]"`), with the latter overwriting the former; they do not define a numeric-key catch-all. Moreover, `z.object` strips unknown keys by default. When credential syncing is enabled, a response such as `{ access_token, expiry_date }` is therefore parsed down to just `access_token` (plus the fabricated refresh token below). Callers then store an undefined/invalid expiry, causing tokens to be considered expired on every request; Zoom can persist `NaN` for `expiry_date`.

findings.title: Sync mode changes the refresh result from provider data to a Fetch Response
findings.body: The sync branch returns the native `fetch` `Response`, while several existing callers expect their provider/axios response object directly. For example, HubSpot reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken` from the returned value, and the Zoho Bigin/CRM services read `tokenInfo.data`; those properties do not exist on a Fetch `Response`. Enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` therefore makes refreshes for these integrations fail or save undefined token fields. The helper needs a normalized result contract (or all callers must explicitly parse the response consistently).

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be a user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId` rather than `credential.userId`. Credential primary keys are unrelated to user IDs, so the configured source application will refresh credentials for the wrong user or reject the request. If IDs happen to match another user, the returned token can be persisted onto this user's credential.

findings.title: Zoom refresh requests use a different app slug than the installed app
findings.body: The outbound sync payload identifies this integration as `zoomvideo`, whereas the Zoom app/credential is consistently identified as `zoom` (for example, the OAuth callback creates `appId: "zoom"`). A source application that routes refreshes by app slug will not recognize this request, so Zoom credential sync cannot refresh successfully.

findings.title: Webex rejects the documented minimal credential-sync response
findings.body: The shared refresh helper documents that a sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but Webex bypasses the relaxed parser and validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. Consequently, a conforming sync endpoint response is always rejected and Webex refresh fails whenever syncing is enabled.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the credential sync endpoint entirely
findings.body: This newly added Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens` or checks `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Thus Salesforce is one of the modified integrations for which enabling credential syncing has no effect, contrary to the feature's source-of-truth behavior.

findings.title: Credential create/update is not atomic and can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The handler performs `findFirst` and then separately creates a credential if none was found. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and both create one. Since the code explicitly cannot use an upsert and there is no shown uniqueness constraint, duplicate credentials can remain; downstream integrations commonly use `findFirst`, making the selected credential nondeterministic. Use a transaction with an appropriate unique constraint/upsert or otherwise serialize this operation.
